ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Scientists have discovered two "super-Earths" of unknown masses, A and B, orbiting the same star in uniform circular motion. Their orbital periods are known to be $T_A = 1$ year and $T_B = 8$ years, respectively.

1. Calculate the ratio of the angular velocities $\omega_A$ : $\omega_B$ of two "super-Earths".
2. Calculate the ratio of the centripetal accelerations of two "super-Earths" $a_A$:$a_B$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Scientists have discovered two "super-Earths" of unknown masses, A and B, orbiting the same star in uniform circular motion. Their orbital periods are known to be $T_A = 1$ year and $T_B = 8$ years, respectively. 1. Calculate the ratio of the angular velocities $\omega_A : \omega_B$ of the two "super-Earths". 2. Calculate the ratio of the centripetal accelerations $a_A : a_B$ of the two "super-Earths".
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Both planets orbit the same star in uniform circular motion, with periods T_A = 1 year and T_B = 8 years. For one circular orbit, angular velocity is omega = 2π/T, so the ratio is omega_A:omega_B = (2π/1):(2π/8) = 1:(1/8) = 8:1. For centripetal acceleration, use a = omega^2 r. Since both bodies orbit the same central star, Kepler's third law gives r ∝ T^(2/3). Also omega^2 ∝ T^(-2). Therefore a ∝ T^(-2)·T^(2/3) = T^(-4/3). Thus a_A:a_B = 1^(-4/3):8^(-4/3). Since 8^(4/3) = (8^(1/3))^4 = 2^4 = 16, this gives a_A:a_B = 16:1.
